source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
- Clearly note the date and time of the inspection along with the weather conditions if relevant (weather can impact some features of accessibility such as water pooling on walkways).
- Record the name of the inspector and any credentials relevant to building accessibility inspections.

3. List the building's basic information.
- Address
- Type of building (residential, commercial, educational, etc.)
- Owner or responsible party

4. Document all failed accessibility checks.
- Use a standardized checklist or form for consistency.
- Include the specific standard or code that was not met (e.g., Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) guidelines, local building codes).
- Provide a description of the failure, including exact location (room number, floor, outdoor area, etc.), and if possible, include measurements and threshold levels.

5. Take comprehensive evidence.
- Photograph or video the exact issue to support your findings.
- Ensure your photos/videos show clear reference points (e.g., doorways
